source.weights: allocated GPU-hours (gpu_hours) of online instance segments, and instance-hours (gpu_hours / gpu_count, replica time) where a field name says instance_hour(s)
source.tier_rule: S: params_b < 10; M: 10 <= params_b < 100; L: params_b >= 100 (total parameters, B)

tier_share_units: share_of_online_gh_with_params: share of allocated online GPU-hours (gpu_count x time, idle allocation included); share_of_online_instance_hours_with_params: share of instance-hours (replica time; a PD-disaggregated replica counts its prefill and decode instances). Neither is a request or token share: converting to one needs the replica capacity kappa_j (design §5.3.1), an ASSUMPTION

instances_per_model_key_per_day.definition: per model_key, mean over its days in the week of (a) distinct instance_ids per day (an instance that ran part of the day counts as one; PD prefill and decode instances count separately) and (b) mean concurrent instances = instance-hours / 24; quantiles over keys weighted by GPU-hours. *_fused: the same over fused (PD-collocated) instances only, keys weighted by their fused GPU-hours; a fused instance is one warm replica

proposed_catalog.definition: window all (days 0-181); params_b = instance-hour-weighted median over all online instances of the tier (fused, prefill and decode; each holds the full weights); g = instance-hour-weighted median gpu_count of fused (PD-collocated) online instances (GPUs per replica, weighted by replica time). The two medians come from different populations: params_b_fused_instances is the params_b median over fused instances only, and params_b_median_mass_point gives the PD-disaggregated share of the median's mass point. The GPU-hour-weighted versions are size-biased and given as *_gpu_hour_weighted; shares in allocated GPU-hours and in instance-hours (tier_share_units); weights at 2 and 1 bytes per parameter (precision is not in the trace); per-block medians in tier_catalog_by_28day_block
proposed_catalog.price_unit_note: GPUs are priced as H100-80GB, so an entry is feasible only if its weights fit in 0.9 x 80 GB x g (a5's usable HBM). On 8 x 80 GB GPUs this holds for 16-bit weights up to 288B parameters and for 8-bit weights up to 576B. The trace's L instances run mostly on larger GPUs (g_by_gpu_memory_class), so g = 8 for L is consistent with 80 GB GPUs only with 8-bit weights or smaller L LLMs

S.basis: instance-hour medians (params_b, fused g), window all

M.basis: instance-hour medians (params_b, fused g), window all

L.basis: instance-hour medians (params_b, fused g), window all; 16-bit weights do not fit on g x 80 GB

M_g_gpu_hours.basis: M with the GPU-hour-weighted fused g (size-biased); sensitivity

L_16bit.basis: L with 16-bit weights and the memory-derived g on 80 GB GPUs (as a5 does for 405B); sensitivity

L_g4.basis: largest L mass point (235B, 0.4174 of L instance-hours) with its fused g; L median in the lender week; sensitivity

field_semantics.workload: online or offline (schema); only online instances enter the catalog
field_semantics.params_b: total parameters in B, not active MoE parameters; NULL if unavailable (schema). Used per row: it varies within model_id and base_id (checks), so tiers are assigned per instance segment
field_semantics.gpu_count: allocated GPU equivalents per instance, fractional allowed (schema). Constant per instance in the lender week (checks), so it is the replica footprint of a fused instance; a PD-disaggregated replica spans a prefill and a decode instance
field_semantics.gpu_hours: allocated GPU-hours of the segment (schema); equals gpu_count x samples x 20 s on every row (checks), i.e. allocation time, not busy time
field_semantics.gpu_type: anonymized GPU type; unknown_ = unknown source label (schema). GiB per GPU equivalent = gpu_mem_alloc / gpu_count is constant within a type (checks), so it identifies a memory class
field_semantics.gpu_mem_alloc: total allocated GPU memory of the instance segment, GiB (schema)
field_semantics.model_id: anonymized source name with class prefix b_ base-only, s_ SFT-only, x_ both, o_ other (schema). Not a unique checkpoint: some model_ids appear under several base_ids and with several params_b values (checks)
field_semantics.base_id: base-model identifier; '-' is a placeholder (schema). Variants per base follow the trace authors' rule (module docstring), which reproduces the README's ~70,000 variants (checks)
